observation_summary: The StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml method incorrectly handles high-unicode characters (those outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, represented as surrogate pairs in Java). Instead of escaping the single character, it treats the surrogate pair as two separate characters, resulting in an incorrect HTML entity string.
hypothesis: The original implementation used charAt(i) which only retrieves 16-bit code units. For characters above U+FFFF, this splits the surrogate pair. The fix requires using Character.codePointAt(str, i) to correctly identify the full 32-bit Unicode codepoint and adjusting the loop iteration logic to skip the second half of the surrogate pair.
prediction: The code will change from iterating over 16-bit chars to iterating over 32-bit codepoints, and the logic will include a check for surrogate pairs (codepoints >= 0x010000) to increment the loop index appropriately.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows a transition from char-based iteration to codepoint-based iteration using Character.codePointAt, and the addition of logic to handle the surrogate pair index increment (i++). This is a fundamental change to the procedural logic of the escape algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic failure in how the string is traversed and encoded. The original method incorrectly assumed all characters fit in a 16-bit char, failing to account for supplementary characters. The fix involves rewriting the iteration strategy to use codepoints and correctly managing the index for multi-unit characters. This is a classic Algorithm/Method defect as it corrects the computational strategy for string traversal.
evidence_used: The diff shows replacing char c = str.charAt(i) with int c = Character.codePointAt(str, i).
The diff shows adding logic to handle codepoints >= 0x010000 and incrementing the index i++.
The bug report describes the failure to handle characters above U+00FFFF correctly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a condition (if c >= 0x010000), the core issue is the incorrect iteration strategy (using charAt vs codePointAt) which is an algorithmic flaw in how the string is processed.
This is a local procedural fix within an existing method, not a design-level capability omission.
